- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for negative sentiment.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 2x recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -1.00), model often fails to adjust; use sentiment transition as trigger to reduce forecast volatility by 50%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a “mean reversion” decay: multiply forecast by 0.85 for days 1–7, then 0.95 for days 8–14.
- When sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–), model often produces erratic forecasts; use sentiment stability as filter: if sentiment variance > 0.5, apply smoothing (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast.
